ChatGPT said:

For an NGO website like Sahyog Vikas Foundation, the homepage should feel trustworthy, human, impactful, and modern. The goal is to help visitors understand your mission, see your work, trust your organization, and take action through donations, volunteering, or partnerships.

NGO Website — Complete Homepage Structure

1. Hero Section

First impression

Purpose: Communicate your mission immediately.

  • Strong headline about creating change

  • Short supporting statement

  • Primary CTA: Support Our Work

  • Secondary CTA: Explore Our Impact

  • One powerful photograph of people or communities you serve

  • Optional verified impact statistics

2. Trust & Impact Strip

Purpose: Establish credibility quickly.

Display 3–4 verified figures, such as:

  • People reached

  • Communities supported

  • Years of service

  • Active programs

Use large numbers, small labels, and a clean background.

3. About the Foundation

Purpose: Explain who you are and why your work matters.

Include:

  • A short introduction to the foundation

  • Your mission and vision

  • A meaningful photograph of your work

  • CTA: Know Our Story

4. Our Focus Areas

Purpose: Help visitors understand your core initiatives.

Use 3–6 visual cards, depending on your actual programs. Examples:

  • Education & Learning

  • Health & Well-being

  • Women Empowerment

  • Environment & Sustainability

  • Community Development

Each card should have an image, short description, and Explore Initiative link.

5. Our Work in Action

Purpose: Show what the NGO actually does.

Feature 2–3 key projects with:

  • Project name and location

  • The challenge being addressed

  • Activities delivered

  • Results achieved

  • CTA: View All Projects

6. Stories of Change

Purpose: Make the impact personal and relatable.

Feature real stories from beneficiaries, community members, or volunteers. Use authentic portraits, short quotes, and the change created by the initiative.

CTA: Read Their Stories

7. How You Can Help

Purpose: Convert interest into participation.

Create three action cards:

  • Donate — Contribute to initiatives.

  • Volunteer — Give your time and skills.

  • Partner With Us — Collaborate on meaningful projects.

Make each CTA clear and easy to access.

8. Latest Updates & Events

Purpose: Show that the organization is active.

Include recent activities, upcoming events, field visits, campaigns, and project milestones.

CTA: View All Updates

9. Transparency & Accountability

Purpose: Build donor and partner confidence.

Include relevant verified documents and information:

  • Annual reports

  • Audited financial statements

  • Registration details

  • Applicable tax exemption certificates

  • Fund utilization and impact reports

CTA: View Our Reports

10. Final Call to Action

Purpose: End the homepage with an invitation to act.

Example headline: “A better tomorrow begins with what we do today.”

Supporting text: Invite visitors to contribute to your mission in a way that suits them.

CTA: Be Part of the Change

11. Footer

Purpose: Provide essential information and navigation.

Include:

  • NGO logo and short mission statement

  • Quick links and program links

  • Contact information and address

  • Email and phone

  • Social media links

  • Privacy policy and terms

  • Registration and compliance information, where applicable

Design direction I recommend

Warm & trustworthy

Ivory backgrounds, forest green, muted terracotta and authentic photography.

Modern & expressive

Cream, coral, deep plum, oversized headlines and asymmetrical image layouts.

My recommendation is to use a modern editorial style with warm backgrounds, strong typography, real community photographs, generous spacing, and one consistent donation CTA. It will feel contemporary without losing the credibility an NGO website needs.

Important: Only publish verified impact statistics, genuine beneficiary stories with consent, and compliance documents that actually apply to your foundation.
